source_text:
2.9 Πρὸς αἷμα
δυσκατασχέτως ῥέον Λαβὼν ἀνθρώπειον αἷμα εἴτε ἀπὸ φλεβοτόμου εἴτε ἐξ ἄλλου
του οἵου δήποτε <ἂν> τύχῃ τρόπου καὶ βαλὼν εἰς ἄγγος πλατύστομον, ξήραινε ἐν
ἡλίῳ καὶ ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ εὑρήσεις ἐπιπολάζον ὑδατῶδες· τοῦτο χρὴ ἐκβάλλειν
ξηρόν τε ποιεῖν τὸ λοιπόν, κἀπὶ τῆς χρείας κατάπλασον <καὶ> ἐπίδησον· σταθήσεται
γάρ, εἰ κἂν δυσκατάσχετον ᾖ.
pass_a_gloss: 2.9 Toward blood uncheckably flowing. Having-taken human blood either from a vein-cutter or from another some of-whatever-kind it-might-happen manner and having-thrown into a wide-mouthed vessel, dry-in-the-sun and on the first day you-will-find floating watery; this it-is-necessary to-cast-out and to-make dry the remainder, and at the need plaster-on and bind-on; for it-will-stand, even if it-be hard-to-check.
pass_b_english: Toward blood flowing unstoppably. Take human blood, either from a vein-cutter or from any other manner it happens to come, and throw it into a wide-mouthed vessel. Dry it in the sun, and on the first day you will find a watery part floating on top. This must be thrown out, and the rest made dry; and at the time of need plaster it on and bind it. For it will stand, even if the flow is hard to check.

choices.why: The lancet or the one who opens a vein. Not a river, and not a job-title forced as the only sense.

choices.english: a watery part floating on top
choices.why: The serum that rises on the first day's sun-drying. ἐπιπολάζω is to float on the surface, not froth.

choices.english: plaster it on and bind it
choices.why: καταπλάσσω is a poultice; ἐπιδέω is the bandage. Not 'shape' or 'mold'.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
